description: Verify that DUT denies a UDP datagram whose Destination Address is the directed broadcast (e.g. 172.16.255.255) — TC8 inverts the RFC 1122 §4.1.1 SHOULD-allow per its automotive security negotiation note
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 1122 §4.1.1 says hosts SHOULD accept directed-broadcast UDP. TC8 v3.0 explicitly inverts this for automotive ECUs — directed broadcast is treated as a security risk and DUT must drop it. This case sends a UDP datagram with dst_ip = directed broadcast and asserts the upper-tester does NOT see a delivery confirmation.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: IPv4 UDP packet
   • dst_ip = directed broadcast (e.g. 172.16.255.255)   ← key trigger
   • dst_port = a port DUT's upper-tester would normally listen on

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester must NOT receive the datagram

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT did not deliver the directed-broadcast UDP to upper-tester.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT actually delivered the directed-broadcast UDP (security policy not enforced)
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue, indeterminate)

verdicts.Pass: DUT denied the directed-broadcast UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for directed-broadcast deny
